response.text:
Stubb’s whale was brought to the Pequod’s side; the cutting and hoisting done. The sperm cooled and crystallized so that, sitting cross-legged before a great bath of it, I found soft lumps rolling in the liquid part. Our business was to squeeze them back to fluid. A sweet and unctuous duty! Such a clearer! such a sweetener! such a softener! such a delicious molifier! After but a few minutes, my fingers felt like eels, serpentine and spiralising.

Under a blue, tranquil sky; the ship gliding indolently; my hands bathing among those gentle globules lately woven; as they broke to my touch and discharged all their opulence like ripe grapes their wine; as I snuffed that uncontaminated aroma—literally like spring violets—I forgot our horrible oath; in that inexpressible sperm, I washed my hands and my heart of it; I almost credited the Paracelsan superstition that sperm allays the heat of anger; I felt divinely free from all ill-will.

Squeeze! squeeze! squeeze! all the morning long; I squeezed that sperm till I almost melted into it; till a strange sort of insanity came over me; and I unwittingly squeezed my co-laborers’ hands, mistaking them for the gentle globules. Such abounding, affectionate, friendly feeling did this avocation beget, that I continually squeezed their hands and looked sentimentally up, as much as to say,—Oh! my dear fellow beings, why should we longer cherish any social acerbities, or know the slightest ill-humor or envy! Come; let us squeeze hands all round; nay, let us all squeeze ourselves into each other; let us squeeze ourselves universally into the very milk and sperm of kindness.

Would that I could keep squeezing for ever! For now I have perceived that in all cases man must lower, or at least shift, his conceit of attainable felicity; not placing it anywhere in the intellect or the fancy; but in the wife, the heart, the bed, the table, the saddle, the fireside, the country; now that I have perceived all this, I am ready to squeeze case eternally. In visions of the night I saw long rows of angels in paradise, each with his hands in a jar of spermaceti.

Of kindred matters: white-horse; plum-pudding—of an exceedingly rich, mottled tint, with a bestreaked snowy and golden ground, dotted with spots of the deepest crimson and purple; it is plums of rubies, in pictures of citron. Spite of reason, it is hard to keep yourself from eating it. I confess, that once I stole behind the foremast to try it; it tasted something as I should conceive a royal cutlet from the thigh of Louis le Gros might have tasted. Slobgollion—an ineffably oozy, stringy affair after much squeezing; gurry—the right-whalemen’s dark glue; and the whalemen’s nippers—leathern squilgees of tail—all pass through the blubber-room, where, by lantern’s gloom, the pike-and-gaffman and the shoeless spade-man hew the sheets—a scene where toes are scarce among veterans.
